metricRule.description: One user-authored threshold rule. A rule states its FAILING condition: the rule fires when `observed <operator> threshold` holds, so `{"operator": "gt", "threshold": 30}` fires when the observed value exceeds 30.

exclude_paths.description: fnmatch globs over the POSIX-normalized relative path. A matching callable is excluded. Callable scope only. `*` also matches `/`, so `src/*.py` matches `src/a/b.py`.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across integrity_rules and metric_rules. It is a component of every finding's deterministic id, so two rules may not share one.

languages.description: Restrict the rule to these languages, matched case-insensitively against the language the artifact recorded. Language and callable scope only: a repository-scope aggregate has no notion of a language subset.

message.description: Replaces the generated sentence for a firing rule. It does not change what the rule does.

metadata.description: Free-form annotations carried through to the finding's rule summary. Never interpreted.

metric.description: A metric from the ArchLens Policy v2 allowlist, printed by `archlens policy metrics`. Every entry names a field ArchLens already persists; NO METRIC MAY BE INVENTED FOR A POLICY. An unknown metric is refused, never skipped.

operator.description: `eq` and `ne` compare exact IEEE-754 doubles; on a fractional `_mean` aggregate an exact-equality rule will rarely fire.

paths.description: Restrict the rule to callables whose relative path matches one of these fnmatch globs. Callable scope only.

scope.description: Optional and redundant: the metric determines its own scope. When present it must equal the metric's scope; a mismatch is refused rather than reinterpreted, because ArchLens persists each metric at one scope only and evaluating it elsewhere would require deriving a value nobody measured.

severity.description: Decides whether firing fails the build; never whether the rule fires. Defaults to `violation`. Only `violation` moves the exit code.

subjects.description: Restrict the rule to these subject_keys. Omit to cover every analyzed subject.

threshold.description: USER-SUPPLIED POLICY. Must be a finite number. ArchLens ships no default threshold and asserts no correct value: this number means the policy author decided it, never that research established it.

rule_id.description: An integrity rule id or a metric rule id the policy enables. A waiver naming a rule the policy does not enable is refused: it would silently protect nothing.

description:
A Policy v2 document: user-supplied thresholds over metrics ArchLens already persists, plus the Policy v1 integrity rules, evaluated together by `archlens check`.

EVERY THRESHOLD IS USER-SUPPLIED POLICY. ArchLens ships no default v2 policy and no default threshold, and `archlens check` refuses to run without an explicit policy file. A number in this document means the policy author decided it; it is never a research finding and never an architecture-quality claim.

NO METRIC MAY BE INVENTED FOR A POLICY. The `metric` enum is the whole surface, and each entry names a persisted ArchLens field. There is deliberately no branch count, no complex-condition count, no percentile, no composite quality score, no maintainability index and no normalized score.

NOTHING MALFORMED IS SKIPPED. An unknown key, an unknown metric, an invalid operator, a non-finite threshold, a duplicate rule id and an impossible scope/metric pairing are each refused at load time. A rule quietly dropped for being unrecognized is worse than no rule, because the gate then reports success while checking nothing.

Policy v1 documents (`policy_document_format_version: "1.0.0"`) remain valid and unchanged, are still evaluated by `archlens policy evaluate`, and are accepted by `archlens check` with the same rules, severities and waivers.

expected_contracts.description: Contract versions the policy pins, checked by the `contract.incompatible` integrity rule. Absent means the policy pinned nothing, NOT that the contracts agree.

integrity_rules.description: Policy v1 rules to enable, by id, at a chosen severity. These are evaluated by the existing v1 rule engine, not a reimplementation of it, so a rule behaves identically under `archlens policy evaluate` and `archlens check`.

metric_rules.description: Threshold rules. Rule ids must be unique across this array and `integrity_rules`.

options.description: Policy-level semantics for data that is not a clean measurement. Both settings are explicit, deterministic and reported in the check result.

on_not_evaluable.description: How a rule that could not be evaluated affects the verdict. `fail` (the default) treats it as a failure: you asked for a gate and the gate did not run. `warn` reports it in `not_evaluable` and in the counts without moving the exit code. There is deliberately no `ignore` — a policy must never report PASS merely because required data was absent.

partial_data.description: How a partial observation is treated. `evaluate` (the default) compares it and stamps the finding `data_completeness: partial`. `not_evaluable` routes it to the non-evaluable path instead, for callers who will not gate on a value that is not verified complete.

waivers.description: Bounded exceptions. Every waiver requires a reason and an expiry: an unbounded waiver is indistinguishable from deleting the rule and decays into a permanent exception nobody remembers agreeing to. An expired waiver stops suppressing its finding and is reported as expired. A waiver never applies to a `not_evaluable` finding, because that would suppress the statement that the rule did not run.
